control_flow.branch_polarity_summary: Every capability bit in this function is a SET-ON-FAILURE bit: the function ORs the bit in when a check fails or is skipped and ANDs it out when the check succeeds. Bit 0x800 is the exception in form only - it is computed from a boolean pair - but it follows the same clear-by-default discipline. There is no read-modify-write of the caller's buffer; the buffer is written once, in order, at 0x0057ade8..0x0057adfa.
control_flow.dominators: 0x0057ac1d dominates every write; 0x0057ad03 dominates both property blocks; 0x0057adc9 dominates the name refinement and the final copy. There is no path that reaches 0x0057ae01 without executing 0x0057ade8.

semantic_contract: Computes a 128-bit capability mask describing what the editor currently permits, and returns it through a caller-supplied 16-byte buffer whose pointer is also the return value. Invariants, in evaluation order. (1) A global bool property, id 0x055D7CA1, read through a runtime singleton, is the master switch: when it is set the buffer is zeroed and the function returns immediately, having touched nothing else - the edit record, the model, the property list and the boolean flags are all left unread. (2) Otherwise the set of capabilities to be resolved is the bitwise OR of two four-dword masks, one derived from the receiver's sub-object at +0x1CC with the global masks at 0x015DA7EC..0x015DA7F8 removed, and one seeded from the globals 0x015DAA40..0x015DAA4C with both that mask set and the first mask removed. When +0x1CC is null the first half is all zero. (3) That request is handed to the capability evaluator 0x004BAC30/0x004F3DE0 together with the current edit-history record, and the evaluator writes the granted subset into the local mask. (4) If the receiver's save extension is crt (0x2B978C46) or cll (0x3D97A8E4), every rigblock of the receiver's EditorModel is queried for a Mouth (0xB00F0FEC) and a CellMouth (0x11B79301) capability; bit 0x400 is CLEARED as soon as any rigblock answers non-zero and SET when no rigblock does, including when the model has no rigblocks at all. For any other save extension the bit is left exactly as the evaluator produced it. (5) If the property list is non-null, property 0x7A926123 resolves to a ResourceKey and the predicate 0x004EFB20 is asked whether the record already covers it; bit 0x40000 is set when the predicate fails and cleared when it succeeds, and it is also cleared when the property list is null or the key does not resolve. (6) The same shape for property 0xF5CBE065 and bit 0x20, with all three failure paths clearing. (7) Bit 0x800 is set exactly when byte +0x4B1 is non-zero and byte +0x4B2 is zero, and cleared otherwise. (8) The part name is finally passed to 0x004EDF40, which may additionally set bits 0x10, 0x100000 and 0x200000 in the first word; its return value is discarded. (9) The four dwords are copied to the caller's buffer in order and its pointer is returned. Additional invariants: the function is not virtual and is in no vtable; it takes four callee-cleaned stack dwords but reads only three; the output buffer is written exactly once, in order, and never read back; two of the callees read-modify-write the receiver's +0x48 field as a side effect, which every observed caller then overwrites; and every capability bit in this function is a set-on-failure bit.
subsystem_context: PKG-10-EDITOR-DISPATCH, cluster editor-core, subsystem Editor, triage GAMEPLAY_LOGIC, priority P3, fan-in 6 / fan-out 11. The function is the single point at which the Creature Editor decides what may currently be edited, and it is snapshotted by the three edit-history operations (Commit, Undo, Redo) into cEditor::field_48..0x54, which is why it runs on every history transition rather than only on user edits. Its dependency on the rigblock capability list and on two configuration properties ties it to the Paint/Parts configuration of the loaded model.
classification_rationale: The body, ABI including the four-versus-three stack argument discrepancy, every field offset, every immediate, the single loop with its exact exit conditions, all thirteen early exits with their polarity, the indirect write through &cEditor::field_48 and the whole order of evaluation are read directly from the disassembly and corroborated by seven call sites in six functions, three of which carry SDK symbols. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for three named bounds. First, the requested bit set is unrecoverable: the eight mask globals and the property-manager pointer all read zero in the static image, so which capabilities are actually requested in the shipping build is unknown - the shape of the computation is established, its input is not. Second, the marshalling between 0x004BAC30 and its own callee 0x004F3DE0 is unresolved, because 0x004BAC5c pushes dword ptr [EBP + 0x8] which in that frame is the wrapper's own return address; the net effect on the output buffer is observed but the hand-off is not understood. Third, no SDK name exists for this method and none is asserted, and the eight individual capability predicates inside 0x004F3DE0 remain opaque ports.
semantic_findings: The Ghidra-inferred prototype is wrong about the stack: RET 0x10 pops four dwords and all six call sites push four, but the body reads only three. The fourth argument is dead in this build.
The function's return value is the same pointer as its first argument, and every caller treats it that way, dereferencing EAX immediately.

The master switch is a global bool property, not a receiver field, and it is the same property the evaluator 0x004F3DE0 checks first, so the early return and the evaluator agree on the kill condition.

Bit 0x400 is the mouthless bit: crt and cll are the two asset types that can have mouths, and the two capability literals are the documented Mouth and CellMouth model capabilities. An empty rigblock list produces the same bit as a full one with no mouth.
Bit 0x800 is a boolean pair, not a property check: field_4B1 must be set AND field_4B2 must be clear. 0x0057eb60 sets field_4B2 immediately before one call, which is how a caller suppresses this bit.
Every capability bit in this function is set on failure. There is no path on which bit 0x20 or bit 0x40000 is left stale, because all three failure paths of each converge on the clearing instruction.

Two callees mutate the receiver's +0x48 field through a pointer, and all six callers then overwrite +0x48..0x54 from the returned buffer, so those mutations are transient in every observed call sequence.
The mask collectors are complementary by construction: 0x0057a9e0 internally calls 0x0057a960 and clears its result, so the OR at 0x0057ac50..0x0057ac68 is belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing.
The function is not in any vtable despite its callers being interface methods, so it is an ordinary non-virtual member; a dword scan of .text, .rdata and .data found no reference to 0x0057ac00.
0x004edf40 is called with the caller's own stack cleanup (bare RET plus ADD ESP,0x8), and its return value is discarded, so its only effect is the three mask bits.
unresolved_questions: Which capability bits are actually requested in the shipping build? All eight mask globals (0x015DA7EC, 0x015DA7F0, 0x015DA7F4, 0x015DA7F8, 0x015DAA40, 0x015DAA44, 0x015DAA48, 0x015DAA4C) read zero in the static image and are runtime-initialised, and no writer was identified, so the requested set cannot be determined statically.

What is the type of the object at cEditor + 0x1CC and what do its +0x24..+0x30 dwords mean? They are the only per-editor contribution to the requested set and nothing in the SDK documents that offset.

What does 0x004BAC30 actually hand to 0x004F3DE0? 0x004bac5c pushes dword ptr [EBP + 0x8], which in that frame is the wrapper's own return address, so the hand-off is not understood even though the net effect on the output buffer is observed.

What is the concrete type of the edit-history record at cEditor + 0x178 and of its last element, and what do the two 0x1d8-stride arrays that 0x004EFB20 and 0x004EF880 walk actually contain? The traversal was read but not semantically resolved.

What are the 0x14-byte records at rigblock + 0xC0C that 0x00435b60 searches, and what is the meaning of the third dword it returns? Only the stride, the key offset and the result offset are established.

What do the individual capability bits mean? For bits 0x400, 0x800, 0x40000 and 0x20 the semantics are pinned by the code; for the other fifteen observed inside 0x004F3DE0 nothing beyond their bit positions is known, and this function's own request for them is unobservable for the reason above.
What is argument 4 for? It is pushed as 1 at five call sites and as a caller register at one, is never read, and may be a removed or defaulted parameter.

Is the SDK's /* 48h */ int field_48 really the same storage this function passes by address to two mutating helpers, or is the SDK's declaration of that offset stale? The address-taken use is observed; the SDK's intent is not confirmed.

What is 0x006a1250's exact contract when the property exists but has an unexpected value kind? Its Ghidra body is mis-parameterised and only the null-list and success/failure shape was relied upon here.
